clue.text: All but the two of us will reject hot drink

parts.note: the two of us will contracts to WE'LL

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone whose friends will all turn down a hot drink, except for the speaker and a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' reverses the hot drink to give NIGH; the apostrophe of the contraction is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old adverb meaning almost or nearly, which is what 'all but' means.

clue.text: Old part of England being captivated by introduction of Windows 10

indicators.note: captivated is held captive, so one piece is held inside the others
introduction points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral 10
esse is Latin for being, as in 'in esse'

explanation.surface: A region becoming hooked on a computer operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: W + X holds ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in south-west England.

clue.text: Al Martino composed something for The Office

indicators.note: composed is arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crooner Al Martino wrote a theme for the sitcom The Office.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Martino was an American singer and The Office a British TV sitcom: neither matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A laminator seals documents in plastic, a piece of office equipment.

clue.text: Ban EU travel until, finally, non-existent

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each word in the list

explanation.surface: A travel ban on the European Union, lasting until it's finally gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Null means having no value or effect, amounting to nothing.

clue.text: Good press extremely desirable for wine department

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Favourable reviews for a wine-producing region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalism; it is ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gironde is a French administrative department round Bordeaux, famous for its vineyards.

clue.text: Where students will be affected: United States!

parts.note: camp means affected or theatrically exaggerated

explanation.surface: A warning that American students are about to feel some change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' reads as a verb but is the adjective, synonym of CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university or college, where its students live and study.

clue.text: One not into unions receiving zero work benefits

indicators.note: receiving means taking something inside
not into says that a letter is removed from inside the word

parts.note: alliances are unions
I is the Roman numeral one
O looks like zero
W is the physics symbol for work

explanation.surface: A worker who dislikes trade unions takes no benefits at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One not into unions' removes I from ALLIANCES; 'receiving' places OW inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are payments made to help with costs, the same idea as benefits.

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking food item

definitions.meaning: a ... complexion is pale and sickly
a ... is a pastry pie, as in the Cornish ...

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking piece of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty serves as an adjective for pale and as a noun for the baked pastry snack.

clue.text: Top of Sca Fell is bare

indicators.note: top of in a down clue picks the first letter

parts.note: tripped means fell over

explanation.surface: The summit of Sca Fell, a Lake District mountain, has no vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sca Fell is in England's Lake District; 'Fell' is a mountain word in the surface but a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means bare, uncovered or emptied.

clue.text: Washing liquid containing red fruit

indicators.note: containing means holding one piece inside

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution used for washing
Che Guevara was a communist, a red

explanation.surface: Detergent with a red fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a colour; it is a political red.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a small sweet Asian fruit.

clue.text: Spain excluded from distribution of air miles, Libya likewise

indicators.note: excluded from tells us the Spain letter is taken out of the pool before it is rearranged
a distribution spreads things around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
LY is the international code for Libya

explanation.surface: A frequent flyer notes that their reward points work in neither Spain nor Libya.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E (Spain) from AIRMILES and 'distribution of' rearranges the rest into SIMILAR; then add LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Similarly and likewise are synonyms, both meaning in the same way.

clue.text: Queen of Hollywood, one providing light entertainment?

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA, and 'of LA' is LA'S
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: Asking about a film queen whose job is to amuse audiences with lightweight fare.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'LA's queen': LA'S + ER, the apostrophe dropped. 'Light entertainment' usually means comedy; here it is literal light, as in laser shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasers produce beams used in light shows at concerts and clubs, a pun on light entertainment.

clue.text: Bird nesting in northern Europe

indicators.note: nesting in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird that makes its nest in the north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: Climbing out of bed after hot cavorting with a new lady at last

indicators.note: after places the out-of-bed piece behind the rest
cavorting is leaping about, so these letters are jumbled
at last picks the final letter of the word lady

parts.note: up means out of bed, as in 'already up'

explanation.surface: A morning romp: someone is up after a passionate frolic with a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges HOT + ANEW into ONTHEWA; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the way up is ascending, which is what climbing means.

clue.text: What can be said of Trump or one like Trump?

definitions.text: What can be said of Trump
definitions.meaning: '...' is true of the name Trump, as it begins with a capital letter T
Donald Trump is a wealthy businessman

explanation.surface: A question about how to sum up Trump or someone like him.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CAPITAL IS T: a statement about the name Trump's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist invests wealth in business for profit, describing a tycoon.

clue.text: Relaxed about extra secure borders

indicators.note: the borders of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is calm about having additional security.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease is a set phrase for relaxed, also the soldier's command to stand easy.

clue.text: Anne Boleyn's deprived of any special honour

indicators.note: deprived of signals that the letters of the second word are taken away from the first
special here means something set apart and done differently, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's queen is stripped of any special honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A, N and Y from ANNEBOLEYN; 'special' rearranges the remaining NEBOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to honour someone by raising them to the nobility, a verb like honour.

clue.text: See 28
Unidentified travelling salesmen

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anonymous travelling salesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nameless means having no known name, so not identified.

clue.text: Arsenal's no 1 policy: to keep current manager ultimately in Emirates?

indicators.note: keeping something is holding it inside, so one piece goes into the other
number one points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: a party line is a policy
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Arsenal's policy of retaining their manager in the Emirates Stadium, their London home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A + LINE holds I + R: A(IR)LINE. Emirates looks like the stadium; it is the airline that sponsors it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates is a Dubai-based airline, given as an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Essentially, Leicester supporters wanting a German left-winger

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, its central letter
wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: angels are financial backers, especially of theatre

explanation.surface: Leicester City fans want a German who plays on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-winger' looks like football; it is politics. E is the middle of Leicester, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels, co-author of the Communist Manifesto, was a German socialist.

clue.text: Cornwall's paradise for the country

parts.note: Cornwall is a county in England's far south-west, abbreviated SW
Eden is the biblical paradise

explanation.surface: Cornwall described as paradise for anyone wanting rural life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as the countryside; it is a nation. Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Second language German? That will cause a row

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: Someone warns that learning German as a second language will lead to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' sounds like a quarrel; here it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy party, something that makes a racket.

clue.text: One called Frank is 13 and reddish-brown

indicators.note: 13 across is ON THE WAY UP, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: Anne Frank, the diarist

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank is thirteen and has auburn hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '13' means the answer to 13 across, telling the solver to read ANNE IS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment and the reddish-brown colour named after it.

clue.text: Endless confusion in European part of the world, here in the UK?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: Asia is a continent, a part of the world

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a tangle is a confusion

explanation.surface: Muddle somewhere in Europe, asked about from a British standpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of the confusion word before it goes 'in' the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is a region of eastern England, so a place within the UK, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Make scratches in roof of shopping centre

indicators.note: roof of in a down clue picks the top, first letter

parts.note: core means centre

explanation.surface: Damaging the roof of a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to mark it with cuts or lines.

clue.text: In communication, 'secure language'

indicators.note: in communication, that is when spoken, signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to tie something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Talk of a 'secure language' for sending messages safely, like encryption.
explanation.walkthrough: THAI is said like TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official tongue of Thailand.

clue.text: Say yes to a female ditched in partnership

indicators.note: ditched means dropped, so letters are removed

parts.note: to affirm is to say yes to

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a woman was dumped within a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partnership' looks like a relationship; it is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business, often a partnership of lawyers or accountants.

clue.text: Record company describes Simpson as an icon

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: EMI is a British record label
O. J. Simpson, the American footballer

explanation.surface: A record label portrays one of the Simpsons as a pop icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in the geometric sense of drawing round; the Simpson is O. J., not Homer or Bart.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoji is a small picture icon used in text messages.

clue.text: Sporting event having would-be scorer?

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A match that features a player who hopes to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' looks like a goal-getter; it is one who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven composed scores, so he is a scorer in that sense; the question mark flags the twist.

clue.text: He investigates lush type, heartless criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so these letters are rearranged
heartless leaves only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A detective sizes up a drunk, a cold-hearted crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves TE of 'type'; 'criminal' rearranges LUSH + TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, someone whose job is investigation.

clue.text: Obsessive behaviour, say, to replace leader of country

indicators.note: this puts one piece in place of the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Romania is a country

explanation.walkthrough: EG takes the place of R, Romania's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself, a pathological behaviour.
